frontier.hypothesis: Under the flip, the loop head's emission order (rows 38-59) can be restored by changing what the loop head COMPUTES rather than how the inner block spells its address - because class C is now known to be a single source-operand-order token whose only cost is that it re-orders the `lw` and the `sll ...,2` in the loop head.
frontier.mechanism: s13 proved the flip is the sole way to reach the target's operand order and that its 24 points are entirely rows 38-59, where the flipped build hoists the D_800A36A0 load ahead of the `sll $a1,1` and postpones the `sll $a1,2` from row 42 to row 50. The target emits BOTH shifts around the load (rows 40, 41, 42). So the lever is anything that forces the `t0*4` shift to be computed early under the flip - i.e. an additional early CONSUMER of `t0*4` in the loop head, or a change in which group first needs it. This is not the group-ORDER axis s12 exhausted (that moves whole store groups); it is the order in which the loop head's three derived values (t0*2, t0*4, the reloaded global) are first demanded.
frontier.next_probe: On the flipped-ABCD body (baseline 29), measure spellings that change the FIRST DEMAND order of the loop-head values without moving any store group: (i) group A's address written `(t0 * 4) / 2 + (s32)base` so t0*4 is demanded before t0*2; (ii) group C's `base + (t0 * 4)` rewritten to `(t0 * 4) + (s32)base` so it enters the integer domain at the same point the flipped inner block does; (iii) the 0x5C/0x60 store pair (which uses t0*2) moved ahead of group A; (iv) the same three on flipped-CABD (baseline 12), where the seats are already right and only the store rows are wrong. Read the resulting emission order with tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s13/ours.py 37 66 and compare against the target rows printed in evidence.md [s13].
